votes.reason: Confirmed from the code at 48d3bb2 without needing to re-run the probe; the sequence is deterministic. `restore()` (infra/runbooks/pgrestore.py:149-169) has no target check at all: it calls `verify(backup)` (checksums only), then `pg_restore --data-only auth.dump` into whatever `--conninfo` names, then opens an autocommit psycopg connection and executes the three NEUTRALIZE_DEFAULTS `alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public revoke all on {tables,sequences,functions} from anon, authenticated, service_role` statements (committed immediately), and only THEN runs `pg_restore -L project.list project.dump`, which is the first step that can fail on a target that already holds the project (`CREATE SCHEMA infrx` / `CREATE TABLE public.*`). So any target with the schema present and no conflicting auth rows is left with its `public` default ACLs stripped after the tool raises; if the source dump has auth rows and the target has none, the auth rows are also inserted before the failure. The only thing that stops the hosted-shaped case (4 users) is the duplicate-key COPY error on auth.users, which is ordering luck, not a guard - exactly as the reviewer says. Nothing in the tree enforces the docstring's 'Into an EMPTY database ... never onto live data' or restore.md A8.3's 'into a NEW project, never over the live one': the CLI (main(), lines 289-292) passes the DSN straight through, and every drill (bk01/bk01b/bk01c/bk01d/bk02 in tests/integration/backend/recovery/test_restore.py) restores into `scratch()`-created fresh template databases; no test restores into a non-empty target and no mutant in mutants_i3b.py (i3bm40-45) touches target validation. The reviewer's severity narrative also checks out: migration 0004 narrows only FUNCTION defaults in `public` (lines 43-49) and grants table/function defaults only in `infrx`, so on a 0001-0009 database the `public` table/sequence defaults are still the template's `{postgres,anon,authenticated,service_role=arwdDxtm}`, and after NEUTRALIZE a new `public` table gets relacl NULL, i.e. service_role (PostgREST) loses default access to anything a later additive migration creates in `public`. Mitigating facts, for the record: the runbook as written (A4 fresh DB from template -> A5) is safe if followed, and the real hosted project fails early by accident; the harm needs an operator pointing `--conninfo` at the wrong database. Still blocking under the stated criteria: it is a stated invariant of a destructive tool with no enforcement and no killable test, and the same task already establishes the fail-closed-before-any-write pattern for the backup side (bk01d/i3bm44) while leaving the target side unguarded. The proposed guard (refuse unless `to_regnamespace('infrx')` is null, `public` has no r/p relations, and each meta auth table is empty, plus a bk01e test and mutant) is small and consistent with the existing drills.

Confirmed from code at 48d3bb2 (infra/runbooks/pgrestore.py restore(), lines 149-179): the target DSN is never inspected - no emptiness check, no source/target identity check, and meta.json (lines 109-114) records no source host/dbname to compare. Order is verify -> pg_restore --data-only auth.dump into the target (line 156) -> NEUTRALIZE_DEFAULTS executed on the target under autocommit (lines 158-161, connect() line 91) -> pg_restore project.dump (line 166). On a target that already holds schema infrx the project restore is guaranteed to fail (no --clean, --exit-on-error, CREATE SCHEMA infrx is kept by restorable() which only skips the public schema entries via TEMPLATE_OWNED), but by then the three ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES ... REVOKE ALL ON tables/sequences/functions FROM anon, authenticated, service_role have committed and any auth rows in the dump have been inserted. The mutation is real on a live-shaped 0001-0009 database, not a no-op: 0004_pilot_roles_and_rpcs.sql (lines 40-49) only revokes EXECUTE on functions from anon/authenticated in public, while the template/shim grants of ALL on tables and sequences to anon/authenticated/service_role (supabase_shim.sql lines 91-96) survive migration - matching the reviewer's measured before {postgres,anon,authenticated,service_role=arwdDxtm} -> after {postgres=arwdDxtm/postgres}; a later additive migration creating a public table without an explicit grant then silently loses service_role access. Test coverage: every restore target in tests/integration/backend/recovery/test_restore.py comes from scratch() which _create()s fresh databases (lines 95-102); bk01/bk01b/bk01c/bk01d/bk02 all restore into empty ones, none into a non-empty target, and mutants_i3b.py has no guard mutant because no guard exists. The only protection is prose (restore.md A8.3 'never over the live one'; docstring lines 152-153); dump and restore share the same --conninfo flag so reusing $HOSTED with the wrong subcommand is a one-token slip. The 'fails earlier with users present' case is protection by ordering accident (duplicate key on users_pkey at line 156), not design. Blocking per the given criteria: a stated invariant of a disaster-recovery runbook tool with no enforcement and no killable test, whose failure path mutates a live database before reporting failure. Reviewer's minimal fix (refuse unless infrx absent, public has no r/p tables, each meta['auth_tables'] table empty; record and compare source host+dbname; add bk01e plus a guard mutant) is the right shape. No live experiment needed; the code fully determines the behavior.

Implementer's layer-1 numbers reproduce: 19 layer-1 cases pass; the 34 layer-1 mutants give 33 killed + 1 control survived, 0 problems (the 7 layer-2 mutants and the rc/bk drills are outside this lens and were not run — no stack was started). Checked claims: Prometheus text is valid under my own strict parser (HELP/TYPE per family, cumulative buckets, +Inf == _count, _sum/_count present, 140 unique series, no duplicates); label escaping round-trips; phase names equal bench.PHASES and the header is emitted in PHASES order — but the evidence cites `models/marlin2b/results/E1B-protocol.md` as the source of the nine names and that file does not contain them (grep 'retrieval' finds nothing); the names live in `models/marlin2b/bench.py:103` and the I3B brief, so the claim is right and the citation is wrong. Tenant hashing is a plain unsalted sha256 prefix, and the docstring says so (pseudonymous, matchable by an operator holding the id) — documented, not keyed. The /metrics gate is the ASGI peer address (127.0.0.1 or ::1) plus absence of any of six proxy headers; verified on a real uvicorn: every proxied form gets the byte-identical 404 of an unknown path, and with uvicorn's own --proxy-headers the rewritten client host is refused too. '20 rules each with a threshold source' is true; 'unmeasured ones are ⚠️' is not quite (PlatformFailureRate). 'Every label is a closed vocabulary' is overstated for mount/gpu/revision (patterns), though no customer-derived value reaches those labels through any call site that exists. No rule reads a customer-visible value; firing alerts carry only component/mount labels or none. No GPU on this host: gpu_up 0 and no memory series — no fabricated zero. No docker, no network, no AWS used.
